card.label: H.R. 7147
card.summary: H.R. 7147 provides fiscal year 2026 appropriations for offices and agencies within the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), excluding U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and the U.S. Border Patrol. It addresses back pay and obligations stemming from a partial DHS funding lapse that began on February 14, 2026. Additionally, the legislation allocates specific funds for the Judiciary and Federal Aviation Administration, and temporarily extends broader continuing appropriations.
card.title: Homeland Security and Further Additional Continuing Appropriations Act, 2026.

card.label: H.R. 8029
card.summary: H.R. 8029, the 'Pay Our Homeland Defenders Act', provides full-year appropriations for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) for fiscal year 2026, ending the partial DHS shutdown that began on February 14, 2026. It authorizes back pay for affected federal employees, ratifies obligations incurred during the funding lapse, and funds various DHS agencies, emergency management programs, and specific provisions for transportation and judicial operations.
card.title: Pay Our Homeland Defenders Act

card.summary: H.R. 7744, the Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2026, provides funding to the Department of Homeland Security for the remainder of fiscal year 2026 and ends the partial DHS shutdown that began on February 14, 2026. The legislation allocates funds for departmental management, security and enforcement agencies, emergency preparedness, research, and training centers. It also authorizes back pay for federal employees affected by the shutdown, ratifies previous obligations incurred to maintain essential functions, and establishes various general provisions, reporting requirements, and funding rescissions.
card.title: Department of Homeland Security Appropriations Act, 2026

card.label: H.R. 7148
card.summary: H.R. 7148, titled the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, became Public Law No. 119-75 on February 3, 2026. This federal law provides funding for the Department of Defense, Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education, as well as Transportation, Housing and Urban Development, and related agencies for fiscal year 2026. It also sets guidelines for the U.S. Sentencing Commission, extends various healthcare, Medicaid, Medicare, and trade programs, introduces pharmacy benefit management transparency rules, and awards a payment to the widow of a late representative.
card.title: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026
